note: The experiments (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 41): what the top bar's "experiments" lists. Each a bench and its tutorial (null for none), named by their paths from this file, or a scene of the optics alone ("scene": "prism", Stage 47); a host reads them and hands the screen the catalogue with each inlined (Ui::experiments, cg_ui_experiments).

experiments.title: Copper from malachite (the demo)
experiments.summary: Decomposition, a gas caught in a balloon, an oxide dissolved in acid, distillation and crystals: the whole demo in 36 steps, with a monitor, a rig and an alarm.

experiments.title: Boiling under a vacuum
experiments.summary: Pressure: steam drives the air out of a flask; stoppered and cooled, it falls to a few kPa, where water boils at 50 C; heated hard, the stopper pops.

experiments.title: Hot and cold dissolving
experiments.summary: Heat given out and taken in: the same copper sulfate dissolved as the white anhydrous salt warms its water by 10 K; as the blue pentahydrate, it cools its own.

experiments.title: What speeds a reaction
experiments.summary: Rate: copper oxide in acid, left still, stirred, or held at 60 C by a thermostat made of a monitor and a rig. Stirring hardly matters here; warmth does.

experiments.title: Diluting an acid
experiments.summary: pH: sulfuric acid diluted tenfold, three times; the pH climbs about a unit each time, and a monitor reads it.

experiments.title: An acid meets a base
experiments.summary: Neutralisation: sodium hydroxide poured into sulfuric acid warms it; the pH hardly moves, then leaps from 2 to 12 within a few mL.

experiments.title: A precipitate
experiments.summary: Precipitation: a base poured into copper sulfate brings the copper out as a pale blue powder; boiled down it turns black, and acid makes it blue again.

experiments.title: A gas from a solid
experiments.summary: A gas: malachite tipped into acid fizzes away, its carbon dioxide filling a balloon, the acid turning blue.

experiments.title: Bubbles of a boil
experiments.summary: Boiling: a beaker heated from below makes bubbles at its floor long before it boils; they vanish in the cooler water, climb as it warms, and reach the surface at the boil.

experiments.title: The water in blue crystals
experiments.summary: Measured: a sample of blue copper sulfate crystals weighed into a tared dish on an analytical balance, heated until white and weighed cold: the mass lost is their water, and the moles of each give x in CuSO4.xH2O. A hand takes about what it aims at; the balance says what it was.

experiments.title: What heat takes from a carbonate
experiments.summary: Measured: green malachite weighed by difference, heated until it is black copper oxide, weighed again: what is left over what was taken is what the equation says, 72 %.

experiments.title: A standard solution
experiments.summary: Measured: blue copper sulfate crystals weighed into a tared volumetric flask, dissolved and made up to the mark: a known concentration. Then 25 mL of it pipetted into a second flask and made up: a quarter of it.

experiments.title: A titration
experiments.summary: Measured: 25 mL of sulfuric acid pipetted into a flask, and 0.100 M sodium hydroxide run in from a burette, fast, then slowly, until the pH leaps past 7. The burette's two readings give the acid's concentration.

experiments.title: The heat of neutralisation
experiments.summary: Measured: 50 mL of 1 M base and 25 mL of 1 M acid, each in a measuring cylinder, mixed in a foam-cup calorimeter; the thermometer, a few seconds behind, climbs about 8 K. The heat over the water made is the heat of neutralisation.

experiments.title: A titration's curve
experiments.summary: Measured and written down: an unknown acid titrated slowly while the notebook logs the pH and the burette's reading each second; the curve's leap is the end point, and its volume the acid's concentration, reported and checked.

experiments.title: Water's vapour pressure
experiments.summary: Measured and written down: a flask boiled free of air, stoppered, its temperature and pressure logged as it cools; ln p against 1/T is a straight line whose slope gives water's heat of vaporisation, reported and checked.

experiments.title: Beer and Lambert's line
experiments.summary: Measured and written down: a spectrophotometer blanked with water reads four standards of copper sulfate at 750 nm; their absorbance against their concentration is a line through zero, and an unknown is read on it. A guess first, by eye.

experiments.title: Rates: the order and the activation energy
experiments.summary: Measured and written down: copper oxide dissolving in acid in a stirred cuvette held at 25, 35 and 45 C, timed by its copper's absorbance; ln t against 1/T gives the activation energy, and half the acid the order in it. A guess first.

experiments.title: A solubility curve
experiments.summary: Measured and written down: four beakers of copper sulfate crystals in water, each heated gently and stirred until its last crystal dissolves; its solubility against that temperature is the curve, and ln s against 1/T the heat of solution. A guess first.

experiments.title: A solution by calculation
experiments.summary: Planned and measured: the calculator works out the crystals' molar mass and the mass for 100 mL of 0.0500 M; about that much is weighed into a flask and made up to the mark; the moles the balance says you took give the concentration you made.

experiments.title: Separating a mixture
experiments.summary: Measured: blue copper sulfate crystals mixed with black copper oxide; water dissolves the one and not the other, a filter paper keeps the powder, and the balance weighs it. A guess first.

experiments.title: Limiting reagent and percent yield
experiments.summary: Planned and measured: the planner works out the crystals and the base for 0.600 g of copper hydroxide; the crystals are weighed and dissolved, the base added in excess, the precipitate filtered and weighed, and its yield worked out. A guess first.

experiments.title: Crystals to a quota
experiments.summary: Planned, made and handed in: the planner works back from 3.00 g of copper sulfate crystals to the malachite; weighed, dissolved in acid, boiled down and cooled, the crop filtered off and handed in against the plan's goal. A guess first.

experiments.title: Supersaturation and a seed
experiments.summary: Two beakers of the same clear, supersaturated copper sulfate solution and a seed crystal for each: left still the seed only grows; stirred, it breeds a shower of crystals and the excess comes out in minutes. A guess first.

experiments.title: Standardising a base
experiments.summary: Sodium hydroxide of about 0.1 M, made roughly, titrated against half a gram of KHP weighed on the analytical balance: run in from the burette to phenolphthalein's first lasting pink. Its concentration from the mass and the volume.

experiments.title: Two liquids, layered
experiments.summary: A gradient: green nickel sulfate over denser blue copper sulfate. Speed the clock up to watch their boundary blur as each diffuses into the other; stir to mix them; a burner under it heats the lower layer. Beside it a beaker of the blue and a bottle of the green: pour the green slowly onto the blue and it lies on top; pour it fast and it mixes in.

experiments.title: Light through a prism and a grating
experiments.summary: Optics alone: a slit of white light in a dark room, seen through a prism of flint glass that spreads it into its spectrum, and a grating that shows its orders. Drag them; the wheel turns the prism.

experiments.title: The lab, free
experiments.summary: The demo's bench with no steps: everything in Supplies, yours to try.
